source.name: Hand-built, checked row by row against English Wikipedia
source.method: enwiki: Cloud, List of cloud types, and each cloud's own article (Cirrus, Cumulus, Stratus, Nimbostratus, Cumulonimbus, Altocumulus, Cirrocumulus, Stratocumulus, Mammatus, Lenticular, Noctilucent, Contrail, Fog, Fallstreak hole, Funnel cloud)

rows.label: Cirrus
rows.looks_like: Thin, wispy white streaks like brushed hair

rows.label: Cumulus
rows.looks_like: Puffy white cotton-ball heaps with flat bottoms

rows.label: Stratus
rows.looks_like: A flat gray blanket covering the whole sky, like a lifted fog

rows.label: Nimbostratus
rows.looks_like: A thick dark gray layer that brings steady rain or snow

rows.label: Cumulonimbus
rows.looks_like: A towering thunderhead with a flat anvil top

rows.label: Altocumulus
rows.looks_like: White-gray patches or rolls scattered in rows at mid height

rows.label: Cirrocumulus
rows.looks_like: Tiny white grains or ripples high in the sky

rows.label: Stratocumulus
rows.looks_like: Lumpy gray-white patches that join into a low, rolling sheet

rows.label: Mammatus clouds
rows.looks_like: Rounded pouches hanging down under a storm's underside

rows.label: Lenticular clouds
rows.looks_like: Smooth, stacked saucers that hover over mountains

rows.label: Noctilucent clouds
rows.looks_like: Glowing blue-silver wisps seen high up at twilight

rows.label: Contrail
rows.looks_like: A white line streaked across the sky behind a high-flying plane

rows.label: Fog
rows.looks_like: A thick, low mist hugging the ground

rows.label: Fallstreak hole
rows.looks_like: A big round gap that looks punched out of a thin layer

rows.label: Funnel cloud
rows.looks_like: A rotating cone dangling down from a storm
